evidence.explanation: C alloc_doors reserves and copies capacity; JavaScript dynamic-array insertion preserves the tested logical door list and per-room slices without that allocation helper. Capacity itself is not an observable parity claim.
evidence.proof: Twelve targets (two boundary-door densities, ordinary/secret types, three interleaved registration sequences) and three empty-map controls compare eight stages each. Exact C alloc_doors/add_door/inside_room/maybe_add_door/add_doors_to_room match actual exported JS add_doors_to_room. Each target reaches 72 or162 logical entries, crossing four or nine allocation increments of20, while every individual room doorct remains0..127. All logical coordinates, room fdoor/doorct pairs and total counts match; repeat calls are idempotent.
evidence.control: Three no-door controls retain empty arrays and zero counts with no C allocations. Targets repeat earlier roots/subrooms after registration and assert no logical change. Three regular root rooms and one regular subroom provide real interleaved slice shifts; source-pinned comparison excludes irregular/shared-neighbor branches, allocation failure, byte overflow, full generation/finalization and runtime doors.
